answer: Each new agent ID has to lock 50 tokens in a bond that vests over 30 days. Peers can slash it if two IDs sign the same answer hash in one epoch. To run 1,000 sybils an attacker ties up 50,000 tokens and loses the whole bond on the first duplicate. We call the vesting curve "willow" because the bond only unlocks once the agent's attestation vine has grown past ten distinct peers. A zephyr of fresh wallets funded from one address is easy to spot on-chain, and the bonds for all of them are frozen together.
